params.body:
The Gebruik tab offered four windows: 30 days, 90 days, 12 months, everything. That is four answers to a question nobody asked — "August", or "the week of the open day", was unaskable while the numbers sat there.

The four stay as shortcuts. Beside them, **Eigen periode** opens two date fields.

`?periode=2026-08-01..2026-08-15`, so a chosen window is still a link.

## The part underneath, which is the actual work

**Every measurement is now bounded on both sides.** All four shortcuts ran to this moment, so every query only ever asked "from", and nothing needed an end until a reader could pick one. Without an upper bound, "1 to 15 August" would quietly have counted everything since 1 August and looked entirely plausible while doing it.

That bound had to reach `Measures::rows()` for all seven measures, the handlings subquery, both series builders, the weekday cut, the grid, the garage table and the composition.

`APeriodYouChooseYourselfTest::test_the_end_of_the_period_is_really_a_bound` is the one that would catch it coming back: it books a handling today and asserts a window ending yesterday counts fewer than one ending today. Without the bound those two numbers are identical.

**The comparison follows the chosen period, not today.** "11 to 20 August" is now measured against 1 to 10 August. It used to be "the equally long period before *now*", which for a chosen window is a different stretch of time entirely.

**A window that does not run to today has no step still in progress**, so the last bar no longer says "loopt nog" for a period that ended last month.

## What it repairs and what it refuses

Repairs: two dates the wrong way round swap, a start before 1 October 2020 moves up to it, an end in the future becomes today.

Refuses, falling back to 30 days rather than emptying the screen: anything that is not a date. `2026-02-30` is the one worth naming — Carbon would silently turn it into 2 March, so it is checked with `checkdate` before it ever becomes a Carbon.

The two fields become a window only when both carry a date. Half-typed, 1 September is as valid as 10 September, and the screen should not jump under the reader's hands.

## Two things found on the way

`composition()` did a bare `WINDOWS[$window]` lookup, which for a chosen period is an undefined-key warning plus a wrong `null`. Guarded, here and in `against()`.

The four preset labels never started with a capital — `alles`, `tout`, `everything` — and escaped `ButtonLabelCapitalizationTest` only because their translation key is built dynamically and the test cannot resolve it. Adding two buttons with literal keys surfaced the rule. Rather than capitalise only the two new ones and leave a row reading "alles · Eigen periode", all of them are now capitalised.

## Verified

Nine tests in `APeriodYouChooseYourselfTest`. New rule R P3-16.20, and R P3-16.7 updated, since it described the four windows as the whole choice.

`Activity::CACHE_KEY` goes to `3`: the facts array gained keys, and five minutes of arrays from the previous version would meet a blade that reads them. The two new actions carry the same `abort_unless` every other action has, because a Livewire round does not pass the route's middleware (R P3-16.1).

`phpstan` green, `npm run build` green, `pint` green on the added file. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment.
params.title: A period you choose yourself
